summary: This article explains why a feathered shuttlecock behaves so differently from a ball in the air, and why badminton demands fast reflexes and footwork from every player.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Badminton: Quick and Light” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: the force air gives against something moving through it, slowing it down
the way a player moves their feet during a game
a very fast, almost automatic reaction

challengeTerms.def: related to how an object moves through air
to expect or prepare for something before it happens

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that badminton needs faster reflexes than most other sports? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Use the words drag and footwork to explain why badminton rallies move so quickly.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review drag, footwork, and reflex, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use aerodynamic, deceleration, and anticipate in a short paragraph that compares two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
